_meta.description: Triangular distribution parameters (low, base, high) for each uncertain input variable used in the reliability engine Monte Carlo sweep. Each entry documents its source status. Variables flagged 'unsourced_assumption' must be replaced with sourced ranges before any external publication of results.
_meta.units_note: All perturbation factors are dimensionless multipliers relative to the base-case value (1.0 = no change). E.g., fuel_price low=0.85 means the sampled price can be as low as 85% of the base-case price.
_meta.sweep_variable_axis: Each variable is perturbed independently in a one-variable-at-a-time (OAT) pass for tornado ranking, then jointly in the full Monte Carlo run.

fuel_price.description: Annual fuel price as a multiplier of the base-case price (coal, biomass, diesel, LPG, gas). Captures price volatility over the payback horizon.
fuel_price.source_notes: Raw data: CIL Notified Prices for Non-Coking Coal (Grade G11, Non-Regulated) from 2016-2024 (2016: 1140, 2017: 1140, 2018: 1250, 2019-2023: 1250, 2024: 1315). YoY Swings: 2017: 0%, 2018: +9.6%, 2019-2023: 0%, 2024: +5.2%. Method: 5-year compounding bootstrap. Sampling 5 years from this distribution yields a p10 cumulative multiplier of 1.0 (0 hikes) and a p90 multiplier of 1.24 (3 average hikes of 7.4%). Asymmetry: The low bound is 1.0 because regulated notified prices structurally do not decrease, creating a purely upward asymmetric risk profile. Derived from 2 observed hike events in the 2016-2024 series; a longer CIL price history would refine the hike-frequency estimate.

production_volume.description: Annual production output as a multiplier of the assumed base-case operating capacity. Affects thermal/electrical demand and hence fuel consumption and savings.
production_volume.source_notes: Derived from MOSPI IIP annual growth rates (2015-2024) for NIC-10 (Food) and NIC-13 (Textiles). Standard deviation of YoY % change is ~12-18% (excluding COVID outlier year), setting realistic MSME volume bands.

solar_capacity_factor.description: Solar irradiation yield as a multiplier of the base-case capacity factor used in system sizing. Captures inter-annual weather variability and soiling losses.
solar_capacity_factor.source_notes: Computed from NIWE/IMD GHI data (2015-2023) for target regions (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu). Interannual variance in GHI totals translates to a symmetric ~±6% capacity factor swing.

electricity_tariff.description: Grid electricity tariff as a multiplier of the base-case tariff. Affects both OPEX for grid-connected technologies and baseline cost for all scenarios.
electricity_tariff.source_notes: Based on state ERC (Electricity Regulatory Commission) multi-year DISCOM tariff orders (2015-2024). Tariffs empirically do not decrease YoY (low 1.0) and show ~4-5% CAGR in industrial categories.

biomass_logistics_cost.description: Biomass fuel procurement + transport cost as a multiplier of the base price. Captures supply-chain disruption, seasonal scarcity, and logistics distance uncertainty.
biomass_logistics_cost.source_notes: Extracted from Biomass Atlas multi-year seasonal indices. Peak vs trough ratio analysis shows up to 40% spikes during lean seasons compared to post-harvest baselines.

capex_overrun.description: Capital cost overrun multiplier. Accounts for contractor variation, civil work surprises, and equipment import cost fluctuations (for USD-denominated technology).
capex_overrun.source_notes: Based on a small sample (n=6) of CAG audit reports on PM-KUSUM and World Bank EE appraisals in India. Shows average 10-18% overruns on civil/installation works. Note: This is explicitly a civil-works-specific proxy applied to total capex, which may understate the variance in imported equipment/procurement costs.

threshold.description: Gate threshold: (payback_p90 - payback_p10) / payback_p50 must exceed this value to confirm the sweep produces a meaningful risk signal rather than a degenerate near-deterministic output. Rationale: a 15% spread ratio means the 10th-90th percentile payback window spans at least 15% of the median payback -- a project manager would consider this a material planning uncertainty. A tighter gate (e.g., 0.10) would pass even near-certain scenarios; a looser gate (e.g., 0.25) would be too strict given the partially-sourced perturbation ranges.
